title: William Orbit, Producer for Madonna & More, Dead at 69
summary: He worked on Madonna's Grammy-winning Ray of Light, as well as releases from U2, Blur and others .
contentText:
William Orbit , the British producer who worked extensively with Madonna , U2 , Blur and more, has died. He was 69.

Related

The news was announced via a statement from his family and friends on Orbit’s verified Instagram account , which said he died at home on July 23. “He will be greatly missed by us and by so many whose lives he touched through his music, friendship and kindness,” the statement said. A cause of death was not given.

Orbit was best known for his work on Madonna’s 1998 album, Ray of Light , on which his signature sounds — which contained elements of techno, trip-hop and downtempo — brought an ethereal backing to songs such as “Frozen” and the title track. The album peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and won best pop album at the 1999 Grammys; its title track won best dance recording at the same ceremony.

The pair frequently worked together over the following decade, with Orbit receiving production credits on “Beautiful Stranger,” “American Pie” and songs on Madge’s 2000 LP Music and 2012’s MDNA .

Speaking to Keyboard magazine in 1998, Madonna described Orbit as “a complete madman genius.” Earlier this year, Orbit put to bed rumors of a sequel to Ray of Light following the announcement of her 2026 album, Confessions II , a sequel to 2005’s Confessions on a Dance Floor . “I have an album ready that imho is indeed the successor to ROL ,” he wrote on Facebook in March. “Everything about how it was made and how it sounds yells that from the first few bars.” He claimed that while he reached out to her camp with the idea, he did not receive a response. “A week later. I speak with many close to her, including fam, but have not had a single syllable back in over two decades. There I said it.”

In addition to the Queen of Pop, Orbit also acted as producer Blur’s 1997 album 13 , which saw the group move away from its Britpop sound and embrace darker themes and a sound influenced by global music. The LP spawned a number of songs that the group would continue to perform over the years, including “Coffee & TV,” “Tender” and “No Distance Left to Run.”

Elsewhere throughout his career, Orbit had credits on singles from U2 (“Electrical Storm,” 2000), All Saints (“Pure Shores,” 2000), P!NK (“Feel Good Time,” 2003), Britney Spears (“Alien,” 2013) and Chris Brown (“Don’t Wake Up,” 2012).

Orbit released under his own name, notably his Strange Cargo LP trilogy from 1987 to 1993, considered classics of the British electronic scene. His 1999 LP, Pieces in a Modern Style , reached No. 2 on the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart, and his version of “Barber’s Adagio for Strings” peaked at No. 4 on the Singles Chart. His most recent LP, The Painter , was released in 2022.

Commenting on the announcement, Melanie C — who collaborated with Orbit on 1999 single “Go!” — wrote, “Such an honour to have worked with this great man.” British dance star Katy B said, “I remember going to William’s studio many years ago, I was so nervous but he was so warm and unassuming and genuinely curious about me and my music I still remember how welcome I felt . What an amazing legacy and major loss.”
